newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds down in muted reaction to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds down in muted reaction to Brazil.

text.p: Argentine bonds were dragged down Friday in a muted reaction to the sharp losses seen on Brazilian and U.S. markets that were reflected across Latin America, dealers said.
Dealers stressed the underlying strength of the Argentine fixed-income market, where losses were minimal compared to local stocks which saw a blue-chip retreat of 1.62 percent.
"The bond market was affected again by the weakness of the stock markets," said dealer Anibal Mansilla.
"But you must keep in mind that the Argentine market is in good shape and prices did not fall too much, reflecting the firmness of the sector," he said.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 closed 1/8 lower at $93.75, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.10 at $118.15.
"It was a tough day," said another dealer. "It wasn't easy to close deals because institutional investors were behaving so cautiously."
